hero.headline: US and Iran sign agreement ending war, reopening Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding to end the war between the two nations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, senior Trump administration officials announced Wednesday. Vice President Vance will represent the US at the official signing ceremony in Switzerland on Friday.

Senior administration officials briefed reporters on the terms of the agreement in a call Wednesday, detailing the framework that will govern the resolution of hostilities and the reopening of one of the world's most critical shipping lanes. The Strait of Hormuz serves as a vital passage for global oil shipments, and its closure had significant implications for international commerce and energy markets.

The agreement has drawn mixed reactions from lawmakers. Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, who had previously expressed skepticism about the negotiations, said Wednesday afternoon that he had a lengthy and productive discussion with a special envoy and now believes the memorandum will be beneficial to the United States. President Trump defended the deal against critics calling for more comprehensive terms, warning that continuing the war could lead to an international depression.

However, Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona criticized the agreement, saying it makes Iran more powerful. Kelly argued that the deal gives Iran resources to build more ballistic missiles and may leave the country with the ability to develop a nuclear weapon. He said the agreement emboldens Tehran rather than constraining its military capabilities.

The signing represents a significant shift in US foreign policy toward Iran and marks the end of active hostilities between the two nations. The agreement comes after extended negotiations between Washington and Tehran, though the full details of the 14-point framework have not been publicly released. The memorandum will take effect following Friday's formal signing ceremony in Switzerland.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as Warsh signals shift in policy approach
cards.body:
The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at its first meeting under new chairman Kevin Warsh, maintaining the rate at a range of 3.5% to 3.75%. The decision received unanimous support from the Fed's voting committee and marked the fourth consecutive time this year that policymakers held rates steady.

The central bank's policy statement reflected cautious optimism about the economy. "Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East," the Fed's open market committee said. The statement noted that productivity growth remains strong and job gains have kept pace with workforce expansion.

However, inflation concerns continue to weigh on policymakers. The Fed acknowledged that "inflation remains elevated relative to the committee's 2% goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy." Current inflation stands at 4.2%, the highest level since 2023, driven largely by energy prices resulting from the Middle East conflict. Even with a reported ceasefire deal between the US and Iran sending oil prices to three-month lows, experts expect it will take months for energy costs to normalize.

Warsh signaled a notable shift in the Fed's approach to future rate decisions. Nine of the 19 Fed officials who submitted projections predicted at least one rate increase before year's end. This represents a dramatic reversal from March projections, when 12 of 19 officials had anticipated rate cuts. Warsh notably did not contribute to the projections, making him the sole board member to abstain.

The policy statement itself was notably shorter than previous Fed communications, though officials did not specify what language was altered. The brevity appeared consistent with Warsh's approach to his first press conference, which ran shorter than typical Federal Reserve chair briefings.

Warsh assumed leadership of the central bank at a challenging moment for the US economy. Heightened inflation and geopolitical tensions have created significant headwinds. While wage growth has slowed to a seasonally adjusted 0.7%, indicating that price increases have outpaced earnings gains, core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, has risen more modestly to 2.9%.

The labor market has remained relatively resilient, with the unemployment rate holding steady at 4.3%. Despite these mixed signals, it remains unclear whether inflation pressures will ultimately convince a majority of Fed voting members to support rate increases.

As a Trump appointee, Warsh faces particular scrutiny from the president who nominated him. Trump previously expressed desire for lower rates, though he stated recently that he wants Warsh to "do whatever he wants." This contrasts sharply with Trump's repeated pressure on former Fed chair Jerome Powell regarding rate policy.

cards.headline: NATO Announces Military Support Increase for Ukraine
cards.teaser: The alliance revealed plans to boost military aid to Kyiv amid the ongoing war with Russia.
cards.body:
NATO announced an increase in military support for Ukraine as the war with Russia continues. The alliance's decision comes as part of ongoing efforts to assist Kyiv in its defense against Russian forces.

The announcement coincided with condemnation of a Russian warship firing warning shots near a British yacht in the English Channel. NATO's military boost represents continued Western support for Ukraine more than two years into the conflict.

cards.headline: Finland Lifts Ban on Nuclear Devices, Citing NATO Alliance Strength
cards.teaser: The Nordic country said the policy change would strengthen NATO as it shares an 830-mile border with Russia.
cards.body:
Finland lifted its ban on nuclear devices, a policy shift the government said would strengthen the NATO alliance. The Nordic country joined NATO three years ago.

Finland shares an 830-mile border with Russia. The government framed the decision as a response to an uncertain security environment. The move represents a significant change in Finland's defense posture since joining the alliance.

cards.headline: Air Force identifies eight crew members killed in B-52 crash at California base
cards.body:
The Air Force released the names of eight crew members who died when a B-52 Stratofortress crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in California. The victims included service members, Boeing employees, and a base engineer who had been marking his wedding anniversary.

The crash occurred at Edwards Air Force Base, a major testing and development facility in the Mojave Desert. The B-52 Stratofortress is a long-range strategic bomber that has been in service since the 1950s and remains a key component of the Air Force fleet. The aircraft was operating at the base when the fatal incident took place.

Among those killed was an engineer described by his wife as a leader and hero. The victims represented a mix of military personnel and civilian contractors working with the aircraft. Boeing employees were aboard the aircraft as part of testing or maintenance operations typical at the base, which serves as a center for aircraft development and evaluation.

Edwards Air Force Base is located in southern California and has long served as a testing ground for military and experimental aircraft. The facility has been the site of numerous aviation milestones and continues to play a role in aircraft certification and evaluation. The B-52 fleet undergoes regular maintenance and testing to keep the aging bombers operational.

The Pentagon released the identities of all eight victims following standard notification procedures for next of kin. Families of those killed received official confirmation before the public announcement. The crash represents one of the deadliest incidents at Edwards Air Force Base in recent years and highlights the risks associated with military aviation testing and operations.

cards.headline: Cybercriminals breach tens of thousands of Fortinet firewalls at major companies worldwide
cards.body:
A group of cybercriminals with alleged Russian-speaking ties has compromised tens of thousands of Fortinet firewalls and VPN systems deployed across major corporations worldwide. Rather than exploiting new software vulnerabilities, the attackers gained unauthorized access by using previously known passwords.

Fortinet's security devices are critical infrastructure for enterprises attempting to protect their networks from external threats and control access to sensitive systems. The scale of this breach affects organizations across multiple countries, exposing the security foundations that companies depend on to safeguard confidential data and internal networks.

The attack method represents a significant shift in how threat actors approach high-value targets. Instead of discovering novel weaknesses in Fortinet's code, attackers leveraged credentials that had been exposed or compromised in earlier security incidents. This approach allowed them to bypass security measures using legitimate authentication methods, making the breach particularly challenging to detect quickly.

The incident underscores persistent risks surrounding credential management and password hygiene in enterprise environments. Many organizations fail to update default credentials or rotate passwords following security breaches, leaving systems vulnerable to exploitation even when patches are available. Fortinet has previously warned companies about the critical importance of changing default passwords and implementing robust authentication controls, yet many customers appear to have neglected these basic security practices.

The compromise of firewalls represents a particularly severe threat to affected organizations. These devices sit at the boundary between corporate networks and the external internet, giving attackers who control them deep visibility into internal systems and infrastructure. Compromised firewalls can serve as launching points for lateral movement across networks, potentially allowing threat actors to access valuable data, intellectual property, and sensitive business information.

Companies experiencing breaches through their firewalls face multiple risks beyond immediate data theft. Attackers with control of these devices can monitor network traffic, intercept communications, and move silently through corporate systems while evading detection. The damage extends beyond the initial compromise, as threat actors may maintain persistent access to networks for extended periods.

This incident adds to mounting concerns about supply chain security and the cascading risks when widely deployed enterprise security tools are compromised. A single successful breach of a popular security platform can affect thousands of organizations simultaneously, multiplying the potential impact across entire industries. The challenge intensifies when the breach method relies on credential reuse rather than zero-day exploits, as many organizations may have similar security lapses.

Organizations using Fortinet products should conduct immediate reviews of their firewall access logs, verify that default credentials have been changed, and ensure that all available security patches have been deployed. Additionally, companies should consider implementing multifactor authentication for administrative access and monitoring for unusual activity on these critical devices.

cards.headline: World leaders express concern over US control of AI access at G7 summit
cards.teaser: French President Macron and Indian Prime Minister Modi raised concerns that the United States could cut off international access to American AI systems.
cards.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi raised concerns at the G7 summit about American control over AI access. The leaders warned that the U.S. could cut off access to American AI systems with little notice, leaving nations dependent on these technologies vulnerable.

Their concerns materialized when the U.S. government ordered Anthropic to disable its most advanced AI models for all foreign nationals, citing national security concerns. The company received an export control directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 without receiving specific details about the security threat. Anthropic announced it would "abruptly disable" these models for all users.

hero.headline: Russian Warship Fires Warning Shots Near British Sailboat in English Channel
hero.body:
A Russian Navy frigate fired warning shots near a British pleasure yacht in the English Channel on Tuesday morning, marking a rare direct maritime encounter between Russian military forces and British civilians in waters close to UK shores.

The incident occurred at 11:40am when the yacht Bright Future sailed within several hundred meters of the Admiral Grigorovich, a heavily armed Russian frigate positioned more than 20 miles south of the Isle of Wight. According to British sources, the Russian crew made multiple attempts to contact the British vessel before firing warning shots after the yacht came within approximately 150 meters.

Britain's Ministry of Defence said the Russian warship fired the shots as an attempt to prevent a possible collision. Russia's defence ministry stated that the yacht was on a dangerous course and that several contact attempts were made, including signal rockets, before the warning shot was fired.

Jane and Alan Kelvey, a retired British couple aboard the 40-foot yacht, disputed the Russian account. Jane Kelvey told the BBC that the Russian ship gave five horn blasts, which prompted them to deliberately change course by two degrees to indicate they had seen the vessel. She said four to five shots were then fired into the air as warning fire.

"They didn't send up any flares, they didn't try to radio us, they didn't look to us like they were adrift, we were definitely not on a collision course," Jane Kelvey said. "We were going to miss them. It just wasn't an incident until the gunfire started."

The couple called HM Coastguard and were later visited by HMS Tyne, a Royal Navy patrol vessel, which confirmed they were safe. No injuries or damage were reported.

The encounter occurred just days after the UK seized the Smyrtos, a Russia-linked oil tanker off the Isle of Wight. The vessel was carrying 98,000 tonnes of Russian crude destined for India. The seizure marked the first time British forces had led the interception of a sanctioned Russian vessel since the war in Ukraine began.

The Admiral Grigorovich is nearly 125 meters long with a crew of up to 220. Its main 100mm gun can fire 80 rounds per minute at ranges exceeding 12 miles and engage multiple targets. The frigate has been regularly deployed near British waters this year, frequently escorting Russian shadow fleet vessels in the Channel and North Sea.

At the time of the incident, the warship was being tracked by HMS Mersey, another Royal Navy offshore patrol ship. British sources characterized the episode as isolated and not directly linked to the tanker seizure, though naval officials warned that Russia may retaliate against British merchant shipping in response to the Smyrtos interception.

cards.headline: Finland Lifts Ban on Nuclear Devices, Citing NATO Alliance Strength
cards.teaser: The Nordic country said the policy change would strengthen NATO as it shares an 830-mile border with Russia.
cards.body:
Finland lifted its ban on nuclear devices, a policy shift the government said would strengthen the NATO alliance. The Nordic country joined NATO three years ago.

cards.headline: Armed Men Storm Hospital in DR Congo, Ebola Patient Missing
cards.teaser: A six-year-old Ebola patient disappeared after armed attackers raided a hospital during the current outbreak.
cards.body:
Armed men stormed a hospital in the Democratic Republic of Congo, resulting in the disappearance of a six-year-old Ebola patient. Authorities launched a search for the child following the attack.

Health facilities across the region have faced repeated attacks during the current Ebola outbreak. Misinformation and fear among local populations have driven these incidents, creating significant security challenges for medical workers attempting to contain the disease.

cards.headline: Israeli Right-Wing Broadcaster Figures Attack Trump Over Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Leading personalities from Channel 14, a network supporting Prime Minister Netanyahu, openly criticized the US president.
cards.body:
Leading figures from Channel 14, a right-wing Israeli broadcaster that supports Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, publicly attacked President Trump over his Iran deal. The criticism represents a break from the network's typically pro-Trump stance.

Channel 14 has been known as a platform for supporters of both Netanyahu and Trump. The shift in tone reflects Israeli concerns about the agreement between the United States and Iran, which includes discussions on Tehran's nuclear program.

cards.headline: Former Nigeria Oil Minister Found Not Guilty in UK Bribery Case
cards.teaser: A jury at Southwark Crown Court cleared Diezani Alison-Madueke of charges she received bribes from oil tycoons.
cards.body:
Diezani Alison-Madueke, Nigeria's former oil minister, has been acquitted of bribery charges following a trial at Southwark Crown Court in London. A jury found her not guilty of allegations that she received bribes from oil tycoons during her tenure overseeing Nigeria's oil sector.

The verdict clears Alison-Madueke of the corruption charges that prosecutors had brought against her in the United Kingdom.

cards.headline: State Department Taking Control of CDC Global Health Programs
cards.teaser: A new plan shifts oversight of international disease work from the CDC to the State Department, drawing criticism.
cards.body:
The State Department will take over much of the control of global health initiatives previously managed by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The plan scales back the CDC's work on diseases abroad.

Critics said the State Department lacks the expertise necessary to manage these programs effectively. The shift represents a reorganization of how the United States approaches international health initiatives and disease prevention efforts.

cards.headline: NATO Announces Military Support Increase for Ukraine
cards.teaser: The alliance revealed plans to boost military aid to Kyiv amid the ongoing war with Russia.

cards.headline: Tropical Storm Arthur forms as first named storm of Atlantic hurricane season
cards.teaser: Forecasters say the storm could generate life-threatening flash floods along the northern Gulf Coast but is not expected to strengthen further.
cards.body:
Tropical Storm Arthur formed on Wednesday as the first named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season. The storm developed near the Gulf Coast from a disorganized cluster of storms that had brought rain across eastern Mexico and the Gulf for several days.

Arthur is bringing intense rainfall to the region, threatening dangerous flash floods across coastal states including Texas and Louisiana. Forecasters expect the storm to remain at tropical storm strength and do not anticipate further intensification as it approaches land.

cards.headline: Long Island serial killer Rex Heuermann sentenced to life in prison
cards.teaser: The Gilgo Beach killer received a life sentence after pleading guilty, with relatives of victims confronting him in court.
cards.body:
Rex Heuermann, a Manhattan architect, was sentenced to life in prison without parole for murdering eight women over at least 17 years on Long Island. Judge Timothy Mazzei handed down the maximum sentence allowed under New York law, which included three life sentences plus 25 years to life on four additional charges, all running consecutively.

Victims' family members delivered impact statements during the sentencing hearing, describing how Heuermann's killing spree affected their lives. The case, which had gone unsolved for years before his arrest and conviction, concluded with the judge removing Heuermann from the courtroom following the proceedings.

cards.headline: One killed in small jet crash along Texas highway as bystanders rush to help
cards.teaser: A small jet crashed near a highway in Laredo, killing Austin tech leader Joshua Baer as the aircraft caught fire.
cards.body:
A small jet crashed along a highway in Laredo, Texas, killing one of the six people on board. Bystanders immediately rushed to the scene and smashed windows to rescue the passengers. The five survivors were taken to hospital in stable condition.

Joshua Baer, founder of Capital Factory in Austin, was identified as the person who died in the crash. Investigators are working to determine the cause of the incident.

cards.headline: Former Nigeria oil minister found not guilty in UK bribery trial
cards.teaser: Diezani Alison-Madueke was accused of receiving bribes from oil tycoons but was cleared by a jury at Southwark Crown Court.
cards.body:
A jury at Southwark Crown Court has cleared former Nigerian oil minister Diezani Alison-Madueke of bribery charges. She had been accused of receiving bribes from oil tycoons during her tenure as petroleum minister.

The not guilty verdict concluded the trial held in London, resolving the allegations against Alison-Madueke related to her conduct in office.

cards.headline: UN human rights experts demand release of British couple jailed in Iran
cards.teaser: Lindsay and Craig Foreman's legal proceedings were marked by grave irregularities, according to UN experts calling for their freedom.
cards.body:
United Nations human rights experts have called for the release of British couple Lindsay and Craig Foreman, who are imprisoned in Iran. The UN said the legal proceedings against them contained serious irregularities.

The case has attracted international attention amid wider concerns about how Iran treats foreign detainees.

cards.headline: BBC to cut 550 jobs as part of 500 million pound savings plan
cards.teaser: The corporation announced initial proposals for 200 job losses in the news division in an email to staff.
cards.body:
The BBC announced plans to cut 550 jobs as the opening phase of a £500 million savings initiative. The corporation communicated the proposals to staff via email.

The news division will bear the initial impact, with 200 positions being eliminated in this first round of restructuring at the British public broadcaster.

cards.headline: Maersk CEO warns Iran fees in Strait of Hormuz would set dangerous precedent
cards.teaser: The shipping giant's chief executive expressed caution about terms of the emerging U.S.-Iran agreement on reopening the Persian Gulf.
cards.body:
Maersk CEO voiced concerns about allowing Iran to charge fees for passage through the Strait of Hormuz, calling such an arrangement a dangerous precedent. The statement comes as the United States and Iran near an agreement to reopen the strategic waterway.

The shipping company is proceeding cautiously as negotiations continue. The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, and any new fee structure could have widespread implications for international shipping costs and maritime law.

cards.headline: Trump administration releases details of proposed Iran agreement
cards.teaser: The administration unveiled sweeping terms including reopening the Strait of Hormuz, waived oil sanctions, and provisions affecting Lebanon.
cards.body:
The Trump administration released a 14-point agreement with Iran on Wednesday, with President Trump announcing the deal at a G7 summit press conference. The agreement aims to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and includes waiving sanctions on Iranian oil sales, allowing Tehran to resume selling oil internationally.

The deal represents significant concessions to Iran. Trump indicated the U.S. would not pressure Iran to abandon its ballistic missile program and acknowledged Iran's right to uranium enrichment for civilian purposes. The administration also committed to returning billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets.

cards.headline: Elon Musk may pursue merger of SpaceX and Tesla
cards.teaser: Legal experts say some shareholders might object to combining the two companies, but would have limited recourse to stop the deal.
cards.body:
Elon Musk is considering a major merger between SpaceX and Tesla, according to reports. The potential combination would unite his electric vehicle company with his aerospace manufacturer in what would be one of the largest corporate mergers in recent history.

Legal experts indicated that while some shareholders might oppose the deal, their ability to block it would be limited. The structure of ownership and control at both companies would make shareholder resistance difficult to mount effectively.

cards.headline: Oil prices expected to remain elevated for months regardless of Iran deal outcome
cards.teaser: Market analysts say oil will stay high whether or not the U.S. and Iran reach an agreement on reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Oil prices are expected to remain elevated for months even as the US and Iran near a peace deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude fell to $82 a barrel following the agreement announcement, but analysts say prices are unlikely to return to pre-crisis levels immediately.

The sustained high prices reflect the need to replenish depleted global crude stockpiles and broader supply constraints. Wholesale gas prices have also declined modestly. The full impact on energy markets will become clearer after US and Iranian officials meet in Switzerland to finalize the agreement and begin a 60-day ceasefire.

cards.headline: Stock markets drift lower ahead of Fed decision
cards.teaser: Major indices showed mixed performance before the Federal Reserve announced its rate decision under new chairman Kevin Warsh.
cards.body:
Stock markets showed mixed results ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision under Chairman Warsh's leadership. The Dow gained while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined.

Following the Fed meeting, bond yields surged and the Dow tumbled 500 points, reflecting how investors absorbed the central bank's stance. Oil markets remained relatively flat as traders watched for U.S. and Iranian officials to meet in Switzerland on Friday to sign an initial agreement and begin a 60-day cease-fire.

cards.headline: Fed statement language undergoes significant changes under Warsh
cards.teaser: The central bank's policy statement showed marked differences in wording, though interest rates remained unchanged.
cards.body:
Chairman Kevin Warsh made notable changes to the Federal Reserve's policy statement at his first meeting leading the central bank. The revised language reflected a new approach to communicating the Fed's policy stance to markets and the public.

The Fed held interest rates steady between 3.5 and 3.75 percent. Warsh also announced plans to establish task forces aimed at overhauling major Federal Reserve operations, signaling broader institutional changes ahead. Officials remained divided on the inflation outlook, with disagreement between those favoring no rate cuts this year and those supporting one or more increases.

cards.headline: FTC lawsuit exposes how subscription scam apps evade app store enforcement
cards.teaser: Federal regulators filed a lawsuit detailing how subscription app operators allegedly use shell companies and payment systems to remain active despite consumer complaints.
cards.body:
The Federal Trade Commission filed a lawsuit revealing how subscription app operators use shell companies and specialized payment infrastructure to evade removal from major app stores. Despite accumulating consumer complaints, these operators maintain their presence through sophisticated corporate and financial structures.

The case demonstrates vulnerabilities in app store enforcement mechanisms that allow problematic subscription services to persist. By restructuring their corporate operations and routing payments through different channels, these operators can circumvent the detection and removal systems designed to protect consumers.

cards.headline: NVIDIA develops AI coding agents to automate robot training
cards.teaser: The company built a self-improvement program that uses teams of AI coding agents to direct how robots learn new tasks.
cards.body:
NVIDIA created a system where multiple AI coding agents work together to autonomously guide robot training processes. The approach reduces the need for manual human intervention in developing robotic capabilities, allowing robots to advance their skills more independently.

This self-improvement program addresses a significant challenge in physical AI development: the labor-intensive work of collecting training data. By automating coding and training tasks traditionally handled by humans, NVIDIA's system aims to accelerate robotic development in a way that mirrors the rapid progress seen in large language models.

cards.headline: Anthropic joins carbon removal coalition with $915 million in new pledges
cards.teaser: The AI startup became the first in its industry to join the Frontier coalition, which secured additional funding for carbon removal projects.
cards.body:
Anthropic has joined the Frontier coalition, making it the first AI startup to participate in the initiative. The coalition announced $915 million in new pledges to fund carbon removal projects that capture and store carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

The Frontier coalition brings together companies committed to purchasing carbon removal services at scale. Anthropic's involvement reflects growing awareness of the environmental impact of AI systems, which consume significant energy during the training and operation of large language models.

cards.headline: AI startup Odyssey reaches $1.45 billion valuation with backing from Amazon
cards.teaser: The company developing world models secured funding from Amazon and other investors in a round that establishes it as a major player beyond traditional language models.
cards.body:
Odyssey, an AI startup developing world models, has secured a $1.45 billion valuation in a funding round led by Amazon and other major investors. World models represent a distinct approach to artificial intelligence that differs from large language models, emphasizing how AI systems understand and predict physical environments rather than generate text.

The funding round establishes Odyssey as a key player among startups exploring alternatives to language model architectures. World models are emerging as the next significant frontier in AI development, offering AI systems improved spatial reasoning and physical world understanding capabilities.

cards.headline: Social media platforms introduce user-controlled algorithm customization tools
cards.teaser: Threads, Instagram, and TikTok are rolling out features that let users directly influence how their content recommendation algorithms work.
cards.body:
Social media feeds are becoming increasingly customizable. Platforms including Threads, Instagram, and TikTok now offer tools that let users directly shape their algorithmic recommendations rather than passively accepting platform-generated content selections.

These features represent a shift in how platforms approach content curation, allowing people to actively signal their preferences instead of relying solely on algorithms to infer what they want to see based on their behavior.

hero.headline: DR Congo hold Portugal to 1-1 draw in World Cup opener
hero.body:
DR Congo earned their first-ever World Cup point by drawing 1-1 with Portugal in their Group K opener at Houston Stadium, coming from behind against one of the tournament favorites in a historic result for the African nation.

João Neves gave Portugal an early lead with a headed goal in the opening minutes after connecting with Pedro Neto's cross. However, DR Congo refused to fold and responded with resilience and attacking intent. Yoane Wissa equalized before halftime with an unmarked header from Arthur Masuaku's corner kick, sparking celebrations on the sideline.

The match showcased a stark contrast between the teams' approaches. Portugal controlled possession throughout much of the game, but their languid pace allowed DR Congo to remain competitive. Cristiano Ronaldo, the focal point for many of the spectators in Houston, struggled to make an impact despite remaining on the pitch for all 95 minutes. Manager Roberto Martínez kept the veteran forward in the lineup, though Ronaldo managed only two half-chances in the second half and a stubbed wide shot from close range.

DR Congo's defensive discipline in the second half proved crucial to preserving the draw. The team's experienced back line weathered Portugal's attempts to find a winner, particularly when Portugal introduced fresh attacking options. Aaron Wan-Bissaka made several crucial defensive interventions, while goalkeeper Lionel Mpassi stood firm when called upon.

For DR Congo, this result represents a breakthrough achievement. The team, known as Zaire during their last World Cup appearance in 1974, had never previously earned a point in World Cup group stage competition. Their preparations had been complicated by travel restrictions, with the team forced to prepare in a Belgium-based bubble before arriving in Houston. The 21-day quarantine imposed on visitors from their homeland had prevented most supporters from attending the match, leaving their backing limited to small pockets of expatriate fans.

Portugal's dropped points complicate their campaign despite entering as tournament favorites. The result leaves them with work to do in their remaining group matches if they want to secure top spot. Manager Roberto Martínez made substitutions throughout the match, eventually replacing midfielder Vitinha with forward Gonçalo Ramos in an attempt to find a breakthrough.

Both teams face quick turnarounds in the group stage. Portugal will seek to bounce back and reassert their status as contenders, while DR Congo can build momentum from their morale-boosting result and push for a place in the knockout rounds. The draw demonstrated that the African side possesses the defensive organization and resilience to compete at the World Cup's highest level.

cards.headline: England face Croatia in World Cup opener with Saka benched
cards.teaser: England began their World Cup campaign against Croatia with Bukayo Saka starting on the bench.
cards.body:
England face Croatia in their World Cup 2026 Group stage opener, with kick-off at 3pm local time. Manager Thomas Tuchel has opted to stick with the team that performed well against Costa Rica in preparation, making one adjustment to include Jude Bellingham in the starting lineup. Tuchel decided it was a close call between Bellingham and Morgan Rogers, and made a slight tweak to accommodate Mateo Kovacic.

Bukayo Saka has been benched for the match, with Noni Madueke included in the starting eleven instead. Tuchel emphasized the importance of having a strong bench, noting that players coming off it can influence and change matches during the tournament.

cards.headline: England take late wickets to leave second Test against New Zealand poised
cards.teaser: Jacob Bethell's two late wickets left the second Test between England and New Zealand balanced after day one.
cards.body:
England claimed two late wickets through Jacob Bethell to leave their second Test against New Zealand finely balanced at The Oval. New Zealand finished day one on 291-7, giving the hosts a foothold in the match.

England's bowlers made early inroads after winning the toss. Joe Root elected to bat first to take advantage of the surface conditions, with the pace attack featuring prominently throughout the day. Bethell's late intervention prevented New Zealand from establishing stronger control, keeping the contest evenly poised heading into day two.

cards.headline: Derek McInnes named Rangers manager, replacing Danny Rohl
cards.teaser: Derek McInnes has been appointed as Rangers manager after Danny Rohl departed the Ibrox club.
cards.body:
Rangers have appointed Derek McInnes as their new manager on a three-year contract, replacing Danny Röhl who left for RB Salzburg by mutual agreement. McInnes, a former Rangers player, joins from Hearts, where he led them to second place this season. He previously turned down the opportunity to manage Rangers in 2017.

McInnes said taking the role is "a real honour," noting he grew up as a Rangers supporter and believes this is the right time to join the club given its current structure and leadership. The appointment marks the end of Rangers' managerial search following Röhl's departure after less than a year in charge.

cards.headline: England make solid start to second Test despite Stokes controversy
cards.teaser: England put in a strong opening day performance in the second Test against New Zealand despite the absence of Ben Stokes.
cards.body:
England made a solid start to their second Test against New Zealand at The Oval on the opening day, moving past recent controversy surrounding captain Ben Stokes.

New Zealand closed day one on 291-7 after Jacob Bethell took two late wickets for England, leaving the match delicately poised. The tourists' strong finish with the ball suggested England were able to maintain focus on their cricket despite off-field distractions.

cards.headline: Olympic medalist Jenny Simpson hospitalized after collapsing at track event
cards.teaser: Three-time Olympian Jenny Simpson collapsed during a track event and was rushed to a hospital in Raleigh, North Carolina.
cards.body:
Three-time Olympian Jenny Simpson collapsed during a track event in Raleigh, North Carolina on Tuesday while pacing a mile group. She was taken to a hospital for treatment following the medical incident.

According to reports, Simpson lost her pulse at the scene but it was restored with CPR and an AED. Event organizer Sir Walter Running thanked emergency medical services and safety professionals who responded to the incident.

cards.headline: Rico Verhoeven's appeal against Usyk loss dismissed
cards.teaser: Kickboxer Rico Verhoeven says his appeal against his defeat to Oleksandr Usyk has been rejected.
cards.body:
Rico Verhoeven's appeal against his defeat to unified heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk has been dismissed. The fight took place last month, and Verhoeven sought to overturn the result through the appeals process.

With the appeal now rejected, the original outcome of the bout stands.

hero.headline: Daveigh Chase, Star of The Ring and Voice of Lilo, Dies at 35
hero.body:
Daveigh Chase, the actress known for her role as Samara Morgan in the 2002 horror film The Ring and as the voice of Lilo in Disney's Lilo & Stitch, has died at age 35. Multiple entertainment outlets confirmed her death on Wednesday.

Chase gained widespread recognition at age 12 for her portrayal of the ghostly Samara in The Ring, the American remake of the Japanese horror film Ringu. That same year, she voiced the character Lilo Pelekai in the animated feature Lilo & Stitch, a role she reprised in the film's sequels and the subsequent television series. Her dual breakthrough performances in 2002 established her as a prominent young actress in both live-action and voice acting.

Beyond her most famous roles, Chase appeared in various television series and films throughout her career. She had roles in shows including Charmed, ER, and Big Love. Her film work extended beyond The Ring franchise to include appearances in Donnie Darko and other independent productions. She also provided voice work for video games, including The Kingdom Hearts series.

Chase began her entertainment career at a young age, appearing in commercials and minor television roles before landing her breakout parts in 2002. Her performance in The Ring helped define a generation of American horror cinema, while her work as Lilo brought warmth and authenticity to one of Disney's most beloved modern characters. The contrast between these two roles demonstrated her range as a performer.

No cause of death has been publicly disclosed. Chase's work continues to reach audiences through streaming platforms and home media, with both The Ring and Lilo & Stitch remaining popular titles more than two decades after their initial releases.

cards.headline: Tom Dreesen, Comedian Who Opened for Frank Sinatra, Dies at 86
cards.teaser: The stand-up comedian known for touring with Frank Sinatra and appearing in Spaceballs died Wednesday.
cards.body:
Tom Dreesen, a stand-up comedian who toured extensively with Frank Sinatra and appeared in films including Spaceballs, died Wednesday at 86. His family announced his death on his official Facebook page.

Dreesen performed alongside Sinatra for years and built a career in stand-up comedy spanning decades. He also appeared in the television movie Columbo: Murder in Malibu and maintained an active performing schedule throughout his life. His family shared the news with fans, noting his appreciation for the joy his audiences brought him.

cards.headline: BBC Announces 550 Job Cuts as Part of Savings Plan
cards.teaser: The broadcaster outlined proposals for 200 initial job losses in its news division as part of a larger reduction.
cards.body:
The BBC announced plans to cut 550 jobs as the opening phase of a £500 million savings initiative. The corporation communicated the proposals to staff via email, with the news division set to lose 200 positions in this first round of reductions.

The job cuts represent a significant restructuring effort for the broadcaster as it works to achieve its broader financial targets.

cards.headline: Latine Immigrant Representation on Scripted TV Falls to 25 Percent
cards.teaser: A new report found that representation for Latine immigrants on television has reached a new low across scripted programming.
cards.body:
Representation for Latine immigrants on scripted television has dropped to 25 percent, according to a report from Define American conducted with the USC Norman Lear Center. The study, titled Change the Narrative, Change the World, assessed 201 immigrant characters across 80 episodes of 62 scripted series that aired between July 2023 and June 2025.

The findings indicate a decline in how Latine immigrants are portrayed on television. The report suggests that the industry cannot depend on a small number of programs to represent the entire community, pointing to a need for broader inclusion across scripted programming.

cards.headline: Sony Releases New Trailer for Spider-Man: Brand New Day
cards.teaser: The upcoming film shows Peter Parker seeking advice from Bruce Banner about losing control of his powers.
cards.body:
Sony Pictures has unveiled a new trailer for Spider-Man: Brand New Day, with Tom Holland reprising his role as Peter Parker. The film arrives in theaters on July 31.

Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, the film takes place four years after Spider-Man: No Way Home. In the trailer, Parker struggles with anxiety about his superhero identity and turns to Bruce Banner for advice on managing his abilities. The footage also features an action sequence between Spider-Man and the Hulk.

cards.headline: Variety to Host Brand Entertainment Event at Cannes Lions
cards.teaser: The entertainment publication will convene executives from Walmart, the NFL, L'Oreal USA, and Spotify for a discussion on brand culture.
cards.body:
Variety announced it will host Brand Entertainment for Fans, presented by Walmart Connect, on June 22 during the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity. The event will bring together executives from major companies across sports, music, retail, and beauty industries.

The discussion will be moderated by Variety Co-Editor-in-Chief Cynthia Littleton and will feature Seth Dallaire, Executive Vice President and Chief Growth Officer at Walmart, along with representatives from the NFL, L'Oreal USA, and Spotify. The conversation will explore how brands operate at the intersection of culture, creativity, and commerce.

cards.headline: Alicia Keys to Perform at Knicks Championship Ceremony
cards.teaser: The New York musician will perform at City Hall following the championship parade on Thursday.
cards.body:
Alicia Keys will perform at a ceremony at City Hall on Thursday, June 18, following the Knicks championship parade. Knicks player OG Anunoby told the musician that the city is asking for her ahead of the event.

Keys, who was born and raised in New York, will take part in the celebration honoring the team's championship. The performance follows the parade scheduled for Thursday.

hero.headline: US and Iran sign agreement ending war, reopening Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding to end the war between the two nations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, senior Trump administration officials announced Wednesday. Vice President Vance will represent the US at the official signing ceremony in Switzerland on Friday.

Senior administration officials briefed reporters on the terms of the agreement in a call Wednesday, detailing the framework that will govern the resolution of hostilities and the reopening of one of the world's most critical shipping lanes. The Strait of Hormuz serves as a vital passage for global oil shipments, and its closure had significant implications for international commerce and energy markets.

The agreement has drawn mixed reactions from lawmakers. Sen. Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, who had previously expressed skepticism about the negotiations, said Wednesday afternoon that he had a lengthy and productive discussion with a special envoy and now believes the memorandum will be beneficial to the United States. President Trump defended the deal against critics calling for more comprehensive terms, warning that continuing the war could lead to an international depression.

However, Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona criticized the agreement, saying it makes Iran more powerful. Kelly argued that the deal gives Iran resources to build more ballistic missiles and may leave the country with the ability to develop a nuclear weapon. He said the agreement emboldens Tehran rather than constraining its military capabilities.

The signing represents a significant shift in US foreign policy toward Iran and marks the end of active hostilities between the two nations. The agreement comes after extended negotiations between Washington and Tehran, though the full details of the 14-point framework have not been publicly released. The memorandum will take effect following Friday's formal signing ceremony in Switzerland.

cards.headline: Justice Department sues New York over Medicaid home care fraud allegations
cards.teaser: The DOJ filed suit against New York State health officials and a company operating a $10 billion home health program.
cards.body:
The Justice Department filed a lawsuit Tuesday in the Eastern District of New York against the state's Department of Health, its Medicaid director, and Public Partnerships LLC. The case centers on allegations that Public Partnerships made false or misleading statements about its ability to operate the state's Consumer Directed program.

The lawsuit targets both state officials overseeing the Medicaid program and the private company contracted to manage home care services. The Consumer Directed program represents a $10 billion home health initiative for New York State.

cards.headline: President Trump settles lawsuit against niece over tax records leak
cards.teaser: Trump reached a settlement in his $100 million suit against Mary Trump over leaked financial information.
cards.body:
President Trump settled a $100 million lawsuit against his niece, Mary Trump, over the leak of confidential tax and financial records to The New York Times. Trump had accused his niece of participating in a plot with the newspaper to obtain and disclose the private information. Both parties announced the settlement through a joint court filing.

The leaked materials formed the basis of the New York Times' 2018 investigation into Trump's finances, which earned the publication a Pulitzer Prize.

cards.headline: Democrats warn redistricting fight continues after Georgia Republicans pause map redraw
cards.teaser: Georgia GOP leaders shelved plans to redraw congressional maps for 2028, but Democrats say the battle is not over.
cards.body:
Georgia Republicans decided against redrawing the state's congressional maps during a special session, citing concerns about the rushed timeline and incomplete understanding of a recent Supreme Court decision on the Voting Rights Act. House Speaker Jon Burns said the state prefers to act "responsibly, transparently, and with ample opportunity for public input."

Democrats hailed the decision as a victory but cautioned the battle is ongoing. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries vowed his party would maintain pressure on Republicans, characterizing the redistricting efforts as a "MAGA power grab." Democratic leaders are working to sustain voter engagement around the redistricting issue despite the temporary halt to GOP plans.

cards.headline: Supreme Court takes up Trump-related cases in new term
cards.teaser: The high court will hear cases involving the former president as well as matters concerning gay and transgender issues.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court has added Trump-related cases to its docket for the 2025-26 term, alongside cases involving gay and transgender issues and campaign-related matters. This upcoming term will feature a significant slate of cases with substantial political and constitutional implications.

The court's agenda reflects the contentious legal landscape facing the country, though specific hearing dates for the Trump litigation have not yet been scheduled.

cards.headline: Mike Pence-backed group opposes children's safety provisions in AI legislation
cards.teaser: Advancing American Freedom joined a coalition arguing the proposals would create privacy risks and limit online expression.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

A coalition that includes Mike Pence's think tank, Advancing American Freedom, is pushing to keep children's safety bills out of a broader AI legislative package. The group argues that tying the proposals to a comprehensive AI framework would create privacy risks.

The coalition also contends the measures would chill online expression. The opposition comes as Congress considers how to regulate artificial intelligence while addressing concerns about children's online safety.

---

Note: The additional source material provided does not contain information about the Mike Pence-backed coalition or children's safety provisions in AI legislation. It covers separate AI policy stories (France's shift away from Palantir, Anthropic's Vatican engagement, and Bezos on AI labor effects). Therefore, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Trump criticizes those seeking broader Iran deal
cards.teaser: The president warned that continuing the war could lead to an international depression.
cards.body:
President Trump defended his administration's Iran deal against critics who want more comprehensive terms. Lawmakers and foreign policy experts have argued the agreement should include stronger provisions on Iran's military capabilities and regional influence.

Trump warned that prolonging the conflict could trigger an international depression. Senator Mark Kelly criticized the deal, saying it makes Iran "more powerful" and emboldens Tehran.
